## What is a Global EOR Service?


A global EOR service is a third-party company that becomes the legal employer of your workers in countries where you have no legal entity. The EOR handles[payroll, taxes, benefits, and compliance](https://www.adp.com/resources/articles-and-insights/articles/e/employer-of-record.aspx) , while you retain control of day-to-day work and performance.


Without an EOR, hiring someone in Brazil or India requires setting up a local entity first, which can take months and cost tens of thousands of dollars. (This is general information, not legal advice. Consult an employment lawyer for your specific situation.) An EOR skips all of that. Your new hire is hired through the EOR's local entity, and you get a compliant, working employee in days.


## How We Ranked Global EOR Services

- Country coverage and depth of local compliance infrastructure
- Onboarding speed, measured in days to a compliant, working hire
- Pricing transparency, including flat fees versus opaque markups
- Payroll accuracy and multi-currency support
- Usability for both admins and employees
- Quality of customer support and dedicated HR expertise
- Integration with existing HR and finance tools


This analysis draws from publicly available information, verified pricing data, and documented service capabilities from each provider.

## Remote


Remote operates through[wholly owned legal entities](https://www.bolto.com/blog/eor-service-providers) in 85+ countries, meaning no third-party intermediaries sit between Remote and your employees. That direct ownership gives compliance teams a cleaner story, which matters in compliance-focused industries like financial services, healthcare, or defense contracting where general counsel often won't accept partner-based entity structures.


Here is a closer look at what Remote offers and where it fits best.


### What Remote Offers


- Wholly owned entities in 85+ countries for direct employment relationships
- IP Guard included at no extra cost for intellectual property protection, according to Remote
- Global payroll option for companies that already have local entities
- Compliance monitoring tools with regulatory change alerts


### Pricing & Fit


Remote charges $699 per employee monthly for EOR services. Onboarding runs 3-7 days, which is workable but slower than some competitors.


The coverage gap is worth noting. At 85+ countries, Remote covers roughly half of what[broader providers](https://www.bolto.com/blog/global-employer-of-record-provider-guide) offer. Southeast Asia, most of Sub-Saharan Africa, and Central Asia are thin or absent. If your hiring roadmap stays within Remote's footprint, that works well. If it doesn't, you will hit a wall.


Remote suits risk-averse organizations in compliance-focused industries where entity structure is a compliance requirement, beyond being a preference.


## Papaya Global


Papaya Global targets enterprise organizations with complex, multi-country payroll needs, offering deep integrations into systems like SAP, Oracle, Workday, and BambooHR that appeal to finance and HR teams. EOR pricing starts at $599 per employee monthly.


### What Papaya Global Offers


- Payroll management across 160+ countries with consolidated multi-country reporting
- Partner-based EOR model using in-country providers instead of owned entities
- Papaya Global-reported proprietary payment rails built on J.P. Morgan infrastructure with five money transfer licenses
- Deep HRIS integrations for enterprise tech stacks


### Pricing & Fit


Papaya fits large organizations consolidating multiple local payroll vendors into one reporting layer. If your finance team runs quarterly audits across a dozen countries, that consolidation has real value.


Where it struggles: partner-based EOR adds complexity in markets where entity structure matters, setup can drag for complex payroll configurations, and pricing stacks up fast when you're only hiring in a handful of countries.


## Oyster


Oyster has built its reputation on making international hiring feel less intimidating, with automated compliance coverage across 180+ countries and a B Corp certification that signals genuine commitment to ethical employment practices. EOR pricing sits at $699 per employee monthly.


### What Oyster Offers


- Automated multi-currency payroll across 120+ currencies with compliance in 180+ countries
- Oyster Shell misclassification protection covering up to $50,000 per claim, including legal fees and settlements, per Oyster's published terms
- Employee onboarding in as little as 48 hours
- Region-specific benefits packages with tailored health insurance and retirement plans


### Pricing & Fit


The $699 monthly rate becomes hard to support when hiring in markets like the Philippines or India, where that fee can exceed the employee's actual salary. For companies hiring one or two people in developing markets, the math rarely works out.


Oyster suits growing companies scaling across multiple countries who want structured compliance support without building internal HR expertise. It lacks any recruiting capability, so you will still need separate sourcing tools before Oyster's workflow even begins.


## G-P (Globalization Partners)


G-P pioneered the EOR category in 2012 and, according to G-P, hires 95% of employees through owned entities across 187+ countries, giving it strong legal depth.


Here is what the service covers:


- EOR in 187+ countries, mostly through owned entities
- HRIS integrations with BambooHR, HiBob, UKG, and ADP
- G-P Meridian Suite with G-P Gia, an AI compliance advisor
- Deep in-country legal expertise across regional labor laws


### Pricing and Fit


At $600 to $800 per employee monthly, G-P is the priciest option in this comparison. The product also shows its age relative to newer entrants, with slower onboarding and an interface that reflects its 2012 roots.


G-P fits enterprises handling unusual jurisdictions, executive relocations, or heavily compliance-focused industries where legal depth outweighs cost concerns. For most growth-stage companies, that tradeoff rarely pencils out.

## FAQ


### How do I choose the right global EOR service for my company?


Start by mapping your hiring roadmap against each provider's country coverage, then compare onboarding speed and pricing transparency. If you need recruiting support before onboarding, choose a provider that includes sourcing; if you only need employment infrastructure, focus on entity structure and compliance depth that matches your industry requirements.


### Which global EOR works best for compliance-focused industries like finance or healthcare?


Providers with wholly owned entities in your target markets reduce compliance risk for compliance-focused industries where legal counsel reviews entity structures. Remote and G-P own most of their entities directly, while partner-based models introduce intermediaries that may not meet your compliance standards.


### What's the real cost difference between EOR providers beyond the monthly fee?


Monthly EOR fees range from $599 to $899, but total cost includes foreign exchange markups, setup fees, and whether you need separate recruiting and contractor management tools. A $599 provider requiring three vendors can cost more than a $699 all-in-one solution - calculate total spend across recruiting, EOR, payroll, and contractor payments to compare accurately.


### Can I use an EOR if I already have employees in some countries but need to hire in new markets?


Yes, most EOR services work alongside your existing entities, letting you hire in new countries without setting up additional legal structures. Some providers also offer global payroll services that run payments through your owned entities while the EOR handles countries where you have no presence.


### When should I switch from using an EOR to setting up my own local entity?


Many companies find the switch makes sense around 10-15 employees in a single country, as entity setup costs ($10,000-50,000) and ongoing compliance can become more cost-effective than EOR fees at that scale. Key considerations include how long the company plans to operate in that market and whether full control over equity, benefits, and employment terms matters, since EORs may restrict some of those options.
